  "summary": "DO-NOT-SHIP. Broker exclusion has a startup race, and the reaper can permanently fail a live job after PID reuse. Two recovery paths also need correction. This was a read-only source review; Windows E2E was not run.",
  "findings": [
    {
      "severity": "high",
      "title": "1. BLOCKING — a starting broker can enter the worker kill tree",
      "body": "The broker is spawned before its identity is recorded and broker.json is saved. During that window, brokerPresence returns null, so cancel or SessionEnd passes an empty exclusion list. A queued worker already has a cancellable PID; its Windows kill snapshot can therefore include and kill its live broker child.",
      "file": "plugins/codex/scripts/lib/job-control.mjs",
      "line_start": 351,
      "line_end": 359,
      "confidence": 0.93,
      "recommendation": "Serialize broker startup and record publication with worker kill selection, refusing the kill while broker ownership is pending."
    },
    {
      "severity": "high",
      "title": "2. BLOCKING — PID-only probe memo can fail a new live worker",
      "body": "The reaper reuses a two-second identity entry keyed only by PID. If worker A exits and Windows gives its PID to new worker B within that interval, A's cached identity is compared with B's record. The reaper marks B failed and removes its PID and request files despite B being alive; SessionEnd may then treat its broker as idle.",
      "file": "plugins/codex/scripts/lib/tracked-jobs.mjs",
      "line_start": 436,
      "line_end": 453,
      "confidence": 0.97,
      "recommendation": "Scope memo entries to the recorded identity and make a fresh probe before a cached mismatch changes job state."
    },
    {
      "severity": "medium",
      "title": "3. SHOULD-FIX — SessionEnd can erase an unreadable broker record",
      "body": "When broker.json exists but cannot be loaded and no endpoint is exported, the hook has no broker PID. With no active jobs it gets a no-pid teardown, then compares null to null and calls clearBrokerSession. A live idle broker loses its ownership record without being checked or stopped, contrary to the unknown-presence rule.",
      "file": "plugins/codex/scripts/session-lifecycle-hook.mjs",
      "line_start": 368,
      "line_end": 374,
      "confidence": 0.95,
      "recommendation": "Clear broker.json only when a broker record was successfully loaded and its endpoint still matches."
    },
    {
      "severity": "medium",
      "title": "4. SHOULD-FIX — interrupt ACK is treated as proof of worker teardown",
      "body": "An acknowledged turn/interrupt is an RPC response, not evidence that the worker exited cooperatively or closed its children. If the worker dies for another reason between that ACK and the attempted kill, this branch records cancelled even when the kill was refused or found the root missing. Any surviving descendants are unexamined, and the terminal record prevents reaping. The descendant outcome is an inference from the race; the missing proof is explicit in this decision.",
      "file": "plugins/codex/scripts/lib/job-control.mjs",
      "line_start": 333,
      "line_end": 343,
      "confidence": 0.81,
      "recommendation": "Keep cancellation pending until a delivered tree kill or a worker-written terminal record proves cooperative completion."
    }
  ],
  "next_steps": [
    "Fix the two blocking races and the record and cancellation decisions, then run Windows E2E cases that force broker startup overlap and PID reuse within the memo interval."
  ]
}

findings.title: 1. BLOCKING — a starting broker can enter the worker kill tree
findings.body: The broker is spawned before its identity is recorded and broker.json is saved. During that window, brokerPresence returns null, so cancel or SessionEnd passes an empty exclusion list. A queued worker already has a cancellable PID; its Windows kill snapshot can therefore include and kill its live broker child.
findings.recommendation: Serialize broker startup and record publication with worker kill selection, refusing the kill while broker ownership is pending.

findings.title: 2. BLOCKING — PID-only probe memo can fail a new live worker
findings.body: The reaper reuses a two-second identity entry keyed only by PID. If worker A exits and Windows gives its PID to new worker B within that interval, A's cached identity is compared with B's record. The reaper marks B failed and removes its PID and request files despite B being alive; SessionEnd may then treat its broker as idle.
findings.recommendation: Scope memo entries to the recorded identity and make a fresh probe before a cached mismatch changes job state.

findings.title: 3. SHOULD-FIX — SessionEnd can erase an unreadable broker record
findings.body: When broker.json exists but cannot be loaded and no endpoint is exported, the hook has no broker PID. With no active jobs it gets a no-pid teardown, then compares null to null and calls clearBrokerSession. A live idle broker loses its ownership record without being checked or stopped, contrary to the unknown-presence rule.
findings.recommendation: Clear broker.json only when a broker record was successfully loaded and its endpoint still matches.

findings.title: 4. SHOULD-FIX — interrupt ACK is treated as proof of worker teardown
findings.body: An acknowledged turn/interrupt is an RPC response, not evidence that the worker exited cooperatively or closed its children. If the worker dies for another reason between that ACK and the attempted kill, this branch records cancelled even when the kill was refused or found the root missing. Any surviving descendants are unexamined, and the terminal record prevents reaping. The descendant outcome is an inference from the race; the missing proof is explicit in this decision.
findings.recommendation: Keep cancellation pending until a delivered tree kill or a worker-written terminal record proves cooperative completion.

storedJob.rendered:
# Codex Adversarial Review

Target: branch diff against main
Verdict: needs-attention

DO-NOT-SHIP. Broker exclusion has a startup race, and the reaper can permanently fail a live job after PID reuse. Two recovery paths also need correction. This was a read-only source review; Windows E2E was not run.

Findings:
- [high] 1. BLOCKING — a starting broker can enter the worker kill tree (plugins/codex/scripts/lib/job-control.mjs:351-359)
  The broker is spawned before its identity is recorded and broker.json is saved. During that window, brokerPresence returns null, so cancel or SessionEnd passes an empty exclusion list. A queued worker already has a cancellable PID; its Windows kill snapshot can therefore include and kill its live broker child.
  Recommendation: Serialize broker startup and record publication with worker kill selection, refusing the kill while broker ownership is pending.
- [high] 2. BLOCKING — PID-only probe memo can fail a new live worker (plugins/codex/scripts/lib/tracked-jobs.mjs:436-453)
  The reaper reuses a two-second identity entry keyed only by PID. If worker A exits and Windows gives its PID to new worker B within that interval, A's cached identity is compared with B's record. The reaper marks B failed and removes its PID and request files despite B being alive; SessionEnd may then treat its broker as idle.
  Recommendation: Scope memo entries to the recorded identity and make a fresh probe before a cached mismatch changes job state.
- [medium] 3. SHOULD-FIX — SessionEnd can erase an unreadable broker record (plugins/codex/scripts/session-lifecycle-hook.mjs:368-374)
  When broker.json exists but cannot be loaded and no endpoint is exported, the hook has no broker PID. With no active jobs it gets a no-pid teardown, then compares null to null and calls clearBrokerSession. A live idle broker loses its ownership record without being checked or stopped, contrary to the unknown-presence rule.
  Recommendation: Clear broker.json only when a broker record was successfully loaded and its endpoint still matches.
- [medium] 4. SHOULD-FIX — interrupt ACK is treated as proof of worker teardown (plugins/codex/scripts/lib/job-control.mjs:333-343)
  An acknowledged turn/interrupt is an RPC response, not evidence that the worker exited cooperatively or closed its children. If the worker dies for another reason between that ACK and the attempted kill, this branch records cancelled even when the kill was refused or found the root missing. Any surviving descendants are unexamined, and the terminal record prevents reaping. The descendant outcome is an inference from the race; the missing proof is explicit in this decision.
  Recommendation: Keep cancellation pending until a delivered tree kill or a worker-written terminal record proves cooperative completion.

Next steps:
- Fix the two blocking races and the record and cancellation decisions, then run Windows E2E cases that force broker startup overlap and PID reuse within the memo interval.
